tests.title: ReadOnlyFileTools contains exactly the six expected tool names including file_outline and find_symbol
given: the agentrun package is compiled
then: it contains exactly ["read_file", "list_files", "find_files", "search_files", "file_outline", "find_symbol"]
the length is 6

tests.title: A read-only phase's resolved tool set includes all six ReadOnlyFileTools and excludes every MutatingTools entry
given: a faux provider scripted with one terminating tool call
a workspace with at least one file
a Phase with BuiltinTools set to ReadOnlyFileTools and ReadOnly true
tests.when: Runner.Run executes the phase and the provider records the declared tools
then: every entry in ReadOnlyFileTools (including file_outline and find_symbol) appears in the declared tool set
no entry in MutatingTools appears in the declared tool set
tests.pseudocode: p := faux.New(toolCallTurn("c1", "submit", {"value": "x"})); r := NewRunner(fauxConfig(p, ws)); r.Run(ctx, Phase{BuiltinTools: ReadOnlyFileTools, ReadOnly: true, ...}); declared := p.Requests()[0].Tools; for _, name := range ReadOnlyFileTools { assert declared[name] }; for _, name := range MutatingTools { assert !declared[name] }

tests.title: A writing phase's resolved tool set includes all six read tools alongside write_file, edit_file and execute
given: a faux provider scripted with one terminating tool call
a workspace with at least one file
a Phase with BuiltinTools set to ReadOnlyFileTools + WriteFileTools + ["execute"] and ReadOnly false
tests.when: Runner.Run executes the phase and the provider records the declared tools
then: every entry in ReadOnlyFileTools (including file_outline and find_symbol) appears in the declared tool set
write_file, edit_file and execute appear in the declared tool set
tests.pseudocode: builtins := append(ReadOnlyFileTools, WriteFileTools...); builtins = append(builtins, "execute"); r.Run(ctx, Phase{BuiltinTools: builtins, ReadOnly: false, Programs: ReadOnlyPrograms, ...}); declared := p.Requests()[0].Tools; for _, name := range ReadOnlyFileTools { assert declared[name] }; for _, name := range []string{"write_file", "edit_file", "execute"} { assert declared[name] }

tests.title: AssertReadOnly returns nil when file_outline and find_symbol are in the resolved set alongside the original four read tools
given: a tool set containing read_file, list_files, find_files, search_files, file_outline and find_symbol
tests.when: AssertReadOnly is called with that set
then: it returns nil

tests.title: AssertReadOnly returns ErrNotReadOnly naming write_file when it is added alongside the symbol tools
given: a tool set containing read_file, file_outline, find_symbol and write_file
tests.when: AssertReadOnly is called with that set
then: it returns an error wrapping ErrNotReadOnly
the error message contains "write_file"
the error message does not contain "file_outline" or "find_symbol"
tests.pseudocode: tools := []core.Tool{{Name: "read_file"}, {Name: "file_outline"}, {Name: "find_symbol"}, {Name: "write_file"}}; err := AssertReadOnly(tools); assert errors.Is(err, ErrNotReadOnly); assert strings.Contains(err.Error(), "write_file"); assert !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "file_outline"); assert !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "find_symbol")

tests.title: toolsNote lists file_outline and find_symbol by name when they are in the registered set
given: a registered tool set containing read_file, find_files, file_outline, find_symbol and a terminator
tests.when: toolsNote is called with that set
then: the returned string contains "file_outline"
the returned string contains "find_symbol"
the returned string contains "no shell" because no shell tool is present
tests.pseudocode: note := toolsNote([]core.Tool{{Name: "read_file"}, {Name: "find_files"}, {Name: "file_outline"}, {Name: "find_symbol"}, {Name: "submit"}}); assert strings.Contains(note, "file_outline"); assert strings.Contains(note, "find_symbol"); assert strings.Contains(note, "no shell")

tests.title: registeredTools calls tools.All per phase, giving each phase its own tool instances
given: a Runner with a workspace
two Phase values each with BuiltinTools set to ReadOnlyFileTools
tests.when: registeredTools is called for each phase
then: each call returns a fresh slice of tools (not the same slice pointer)
both slices contain file_outline and find_symbol
no code change to registeredTools is needed — the existing per-phase tools.All call provides freshness
tests.pseudocode: r := NewRunner(cfg); p1 := Phase{BuiltinTools: ReadOnlyFileTools, ReadOnly: true}; p2 := Phase{BuiltinTools: ReadOnlyFileTools, ReadOnly: true}; t1, _ := r.registeredTools(p1); t2, _ := r.registeredTools(p2); assert &t1 != &t2; assert contains(t1, "file_outline"); assert contains(t2, "find_symbol")

tests.title: registeredTools passes tools.Options with zero-value Symbols field
given: the source of registeredTools in internal/agentrun/phase.go
tests.when: the tools.All call site is inspected
then: tools.Options is constructed with only Workspace set
no Symbols field is set (it uses the zero value / AgentKit defaults)
tests.pseudocode: // Source inspection: the call is tools.All(tools.Options{Workspace: r.cfg.Workspace}); assert no Symbols field is set in the Options literal

tests.title: Each RunPreflight adds a symbol_backend check with OK true and detail 'ctags' or 'heuristics'
given: a workspace pointing to a valid git repository
a Runner configured with a faux provider
the four RunPreflight functions: codefix, codeimpl, specgen, issuetriage
tests.when: each RunPreflight is called with valid options
then: the returned result's Preflight list contains an entry with Check "symbol_backend"
that entry's OK is true
that entry's Detail is either "ctags" or "heuristics"
tests.pseudocode: for _, runPF := range [codefix.RunPreflight, codeimpl.RunPreflight, specgen.RunPreflight, issuetriage.RunPreflight] { res, err := runPF(ctx, opts); assert err == nil; found := false; for _, c := range res.Preflight { if c.Check == "symbol_backend" { found = true; assert c.OK == true; assert c.Detail == "ctags" || c.Detail == "heuristics" } }; assert found }

tests.title: RunPreflight omits the symbol_backend check when detection fails rather than failing the preflight
given: a RunPreflight function called with options where the workspace is nil or tools.All returns an error for symbol detection
tests.when: RunPreflight is called and the ctags detection mechanism fails
then: the returned PreflightCheck list contains no entry with Check "symbol_backend"
the preflight result is otherwise unaffected — other checks are still present
no error is returned from RunPreflight due to the detection failure
tests.pseudocode: // Simulate detection failure (e.g. tools.All returns error for symbol detection); res, err := RunPreflight(ctx, opts); assert err == nil || err is from another check; for _, c := range res.Preflight { assert c.Check != "symbol_backend" }

tests.title: The repo map's opening sentence mentions file_outline and find_symbol
given: the repo map rendering function in internal/repomap or the prompt function that renders the repo map block
tests.when: the repo map is rendered for any phase
then: the opening sentence contains "file_outline"
the opening sentence contains "find_symbol"
the opening sentence contains "Use `read_file` with `offset`/`limit` to read a declaration, `file_outline` for a file's full outline, and `find_symbol` to locate a name across the repository."
the opening sentence contains "Use `find_files` and `search_files` for anything the map does not show."
tests.pseudocode: rendered := renderRepoMap(ws, budget); assert strings.Contains(rendered, "`file_outline` for a file's full outline"); assert strings.Contains(rendered, "`find_symbol` to locate a name across the repository")

tests.title: docs/model-usage.md lists all six read tools in the phase table
given: docs/model-usage.md exists
then: every row that previously said 'the four read tools' now says 'the six read tools' or lists all six
file_outline and find_symbol appear in the tool lists for issue/triage, fix/analyse, fix/implement, all spec phases, impl/survey, impl/repair and impl/implement

tests.title: docs/model-usage.md describes the symbol tools in the 'Reading the codebase' section
given: docs/model-usage.md exists
tests.when: the 'Reading the codebase' section is read
then: it describes what file_outline does

tests.pseudocode: content := readFile("docs/model-usage.md"); section := extractSection(content, "Reading the codebase"); assert strings.Contains(section, "file_outline"); assert strings.Contains(section, "find_symbol"); assert strings.Contains(section, "ctags"); assert strings.Contains(section, "heuristics"); assert strings.Contains(section, "symbol table")
